decision: Deferred: both implementations pass focused correctness checks but do not demonstrate a convincing compilation latency gain. Original emitter retained.

resize.patch:
diff --git a/core/compiler/x64.jo b/core/compiler/x64.jo
index 4702fa01..b1fb0358 100644
--- a/core/compiler/x64.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/x64.jo
@@ -31,19 +31,22 @@ data_fix: (int, int, int)[]  # (position of rel32, kind 0=rodata 1=data, offset)
 int_arg_regs = [RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9]
 
 b = (x: int): code.push(u8(x & 255))
+# Supported compiler hosts are little-endian x86-64 and ARM64, both allowing
+# unaligned integer stores. Grow once per word; data() preserves copy-on-write.
 b32 = (x: int):
-    b(x)
-    b(x >> 8)
-    b(x >> 16)
-    b(x >> 24)
+    at = code.len()
+    code.resize(at + 4)
+    p = (code.data() + at) as *i32
+    p[0] = i32(x)
 b64 = (x: int):
-    b32(x)
-    b32(x >> 32)
+    at = code.len()
+    code.resize(at + 8)
+    p = (code.data() + at) as *int
+    p[0] = x
 patch32 = (pos: int, v: int):
-    code[pos] = u8(v & 255)
-    code[pos + 1] = u8((v >> 8) & 255)
-    code[pos + 2] = u8((v >> 16) & 255)
-    code[pos + 3] = u8((v >> 24) & 255)
+    if pos < 0 or pos > code.len() - 4: panic("invalid x86-64 code fixup")
+    p = (code.data() + pos) as *i32
+    p[0] = i32(v)
 
 rip_kind = 0
 # index register for the next memory operand ([base + index << scale + disp]); -1: none
